simple.meaning: מַמְזֵר (mamzêr) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a mongrel , i.e. born of a Jewish father and a heathen mother.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Deuteronomy 23:3. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַמְזֵר (H4464) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַמְזֵר (mamzêr) / H4464 is traced through Deuteronomy 23:3, Zechariah 9:6 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: a mongrel , i.e. born of a Jewish father and a heathen mother
definitions.full: H4464. mamzer מַמְזֵר noun masculine bastard , specifically child of incest (Late Hebrew id. (see Levy), מַמְזֵרוּת incest ; Aramaic (loan-word) מַמְזֵרָא bastard ): — 1 literally bastard , Deut 23:3 (see Dr). 2 perhaps figurative collective, of mixed population Zech 9:6 ᵐ5 ἀλλογενεῖς (compare also Gei Urschrift 52f. ) II. מזר (√ of following, si vera lectio; possibly = spread out ; Aramaic stretch oneself , compare Arabic aequaliter distendit utrem).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to alienate ;
